evidence.section: Edit Distance in Bioinformatics and Sequence Analysis
evidence.excerpt: Edit distance provides a foundational model for comparing biological and synthetic sequences through insertions, deletions, and substitutions, but biological sequence analysis often requires richer assumptions than ordinary unit-cost Levenshtein distance can express. This section examines where edit distance fits in bioinformatics, how it relates to sequence alignment and gap models, why bounded edit distance is important in genomic search and read mapping, and how insertion, deletion, and substitution errors arise in emerging systems such as DNA data storage. The emphasis is on distinguishing generic sequence-edit similarity from biologically meaningful scoring, alignment, and inference.
